idea: Signs of a hidden water leak
title: Using a Water Meter to Confirm Hidden Leaks
description: Learn how to use the low-flow indicator dial on a water meter to diagnose concealed water supply leaks.
image_prompt: Photorealistic vertical 9:16 photograph of a brass mechanical water meter connected to a clean copper water main line in a basement utility space. Crisp focus on the clear glass dial face of the water meter, displaying mechanical register numbers and a bright red triangular low-flow leak detector dial. Clean metallic pipe textures, realistic brass threaded fittings, and directional flow markings on the meter body. Softly blurred wall background with neutral overhead lighting, leaving clear open space in the upper and lower thirds of the frame for text overlays. No text, no watermarks, no logos, no fake brand names, no graphics.
visual_story: The visual focuses directly on the face of a standard mechanical water meter, highlighting the low-flow indicator spinner. The image teaches viewers where to inspect on the meter dial to verify whether water is actively flowing through the pressurized supply line when no taps are open.

on_image_text.hook: How to Confirm a Hidden Water Leak
on_image_text.explanation: If all fixtures are off and this dial rotates, water is escaping the pressurized line.
on_image_text.takeaway: Isolate individual branch valves to locate the leaking section.
